verses.1: My son, do not forget my instruction; let my commandments guard your heart.
verses.2: For they add to you long life, years of life, and peace.
verses.3: Let steadfast love and truth not leave you; bind them around your neck, inscribe them on the tablet of your heart.
verses.4: Then you will find favor and good understanding in the eyes of God and of human beings.
verses.5: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not rely on your own understanding.
verses.6: In all your ways know him, and he will make straight your paths.
verses.7: Do not consider yourself wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and turn away from evil.
verses.8: It will be healing for your flesh and refreshment for your bones.
verses.9: Honor the LORD from your wealth, and from the first of all your produce.
verses.10: Then your storehouses will be filled with abundance, and your wine vats will overflow.
verses.11: My son, do not despise the discipline of the LORD, nor be resentful when he rebukes you.
verses.12: For the one whom the LORD loves, he instructs; like a father, he disciplines a child.
verses.13: Happy is the one who finds wisdom, and the one who gains understanding.
verses.14: For her value is better than silver, and her gain is better than gold.
verses.15: She is more precious than pearls, and nothing you desire can compare with her.
verses.16: Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor.
verses.17: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.
verses.18: She is a tree of life to those who hold her, and those who support her are blessed.
verses.19: The LORD founded the earth in wisdom, and he established the heavens with understanding.
verses.20: By his knowledge the deeps were split open, and the clouds drop down dew.
verses.21: My son, let not insight and discernment leave your eyes.
verses.22: Let them be life to your soul and grace to your throat.
verses.23: Then you will walk with assurance in your steps, and your foot will not stumble.
verses.24: If you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you lie down, your sleep will be sweet.
verses.25: Have no fear of sudden terror or of the onslaught of the wicked when it comes.
verses.26: For the LORD will be your confidence, and he will guard your foot from snaring.
verses.27: Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to act.
verses.28: Do not say to your neighbor, "Go, and come back, and tomorrow I will give," when you have it with you now.
verses.29: Do not plot evil against your neighbor, who lives in safety with you.
verses.30: Do not contend with a man for no reason, if he has done you no harm.
verses.31: Do not envy a violent man, and do not choose any of his ways.
verses.32: For the LORD rejects the perverse, but with the upright he is in counsel.
verses.33: The curse of the LORD is in the house of the wicked, but the tents of the righteous he blesses.
verses.34: He mocks the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
verses.35: The wise will inherit glory, but the foolish carry shame.

notes:
Notes
- v. 20: The phrase "the deeps were split open" reflects the poetic metaphor for the creation of the firmament and the separation of waters. "Drop down dew" is a poetic rendering of the clouds releasing moisture, rather than a literal meteorological description.
- v. 34: The Hebrew uses a wordplay between arrogance (גְּאוֹן) and grace (חֵן), which is preserved in the poetic contrast between "he mocks the proud" and "gives grace to the humble."
- v. 35: "Carry shame" is a metaphor for bearing disgrace, which is consistent with the parallel structure and the overall theme of the chapter.
